description: Violet, forked white to the shell, dropped by a Stormcrown. The air near it tastes like a coming storm.
lore: The sceptics' line about [[monsters/storm_stag|the stag]] is older than most of the people saying it: a tall thing on a summit in bad weather gets hit, and that is geometry, not character. A rod with legs, and the rest is people wanting a story out of a hill.

The stone is the answer, and not the one they wanted. A stone carries one fact and no more, and this one's is not a thing that was struck. It is a thing that was come to. Violet plates forked white to the shell, working out from a white middle, and the hair lifts on your forearm the moment you take it up. In a fight it does not count one body a finished job: the hit lands, and then it is in the next thing along, and then it has done.

Two hundred and seventy gold, and the rest of the cost is the part nobody prices out loud. The weather that brings the lightning is the weather you have to stand in, so being broken up there is part of the errand rather than a mishap in it, and what re-forms beside the nearest tended fire is short a little of whatever it had been thinking. Ask a seller how he came by his and the answer is honest, cheerful and incomplete, and he does not know it is incomplete.

A stone cannot be forgotten. Everywhere else in the trade that is a remark about value. Up there it means something narrower: whatever else goes out of a man's head on the way down, the stone in his fist is the one part of the errand that comes back entire.
gm_notes: The creature's record owns the woman who climbs up and Solveig's nine meetings; neither is restaged, and the walk down is reached from the sellers' side instead. Struck versus come to is what only the stone can settle, and it settles it against the sceptics. The arc is written as a habit of the fact, not as the danger-to-your-friend beat that cyan_lightning_egg owns.
